Emily — thanks for the detailed questions and the questionnaire. Quick answers to start:

- We typically publish 12/24/36-month private offer pricing tiers; discounts scale with committed ARR and term length. I attached an initial quote to give you a ballpark.
- Internally, discounts above ~30% trigger review by our pricing committee; anything >40% requires VP sales signoff and legal review. I will confirm exact thresholds with Vanessa.

Could you share expected annual committed spend or estimated monthly usage so Vanessa can model tiers?

Subject: Pricing models and approval path for BrightWare private offer

Hi Emily / team — looping in an initial pricing breakdown based on common commitment bands. These are illustrative until we get your expected committed spend: 

- Band A (committed spend < $100k/yr): 0%–10% discount (12/24/36 month options)
- Band B ($100k–$500k/yr): 10%–25% discount
- Band C ($500k–$2M/yr): 25%–35% discount
- Band D (> $2M/yr): 35%–45% discount (requires pricing committee review)

Term effects: longer terms (36mo) move you ~5–8% deeper into the top of the band vs 12mo.

Approval notes (internal): discounts above 30% => pricing committee; above 40% => VP Sales + Legal. For term lengths >24 months we ask Legal to confirm auto-renew and data-retention language.

Procurement flow we recommend:
1) Buyer confirms committed spend band and signs the quote (DocuSign).
2) Redwood submits private offer in AWS Seller Central, referencing the DocuSign/PO.
3) Buyer accepts private offer via their AWS Marketplace console, then PO/Invoice flow completes.

I've attached a spreadsheet with example scenarios (pricing-models.xlsx). If you can share your expected annualized spend, we’ll produce a final quote.

Thanks — happy to jump on a working session if helpful.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-models.xlsx (Excel)
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com

Adding operational approvals and a suggested checklist so we don't hit last-minute delays: 

- If final discount > 35%: require pricing committee memo + documented competitor benchmark.
- If term >= 36 months: Legal to review auto-renew and termination for convenience clauses.
- For any deal where buyer requires data residency guarantees: engage Security (SOC2 artifact attached).
- AWS-specific: ensure private offer metadata includes our AWS Seller ID and the HubSpot deal ID so Procurement can reconcile.

Suggested internal signoff path (fast lane):
1) AE (laura_bennett) confirms committed spend band and stakeholder (BrightWare PO contact).
2) VP Sales (or delegate) approves discount >30%.
3) Pricing committee signs off if >35%.
4) Legal reviews term language if term >24 months.
5) Sales Ops (marcus_lin) submits private offer to AWS with attachments (quote + signed DocuSign).

I'll prepare the pricing committee memo template if we get to >35%. HubSpot reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7800/DEAL-BW-2026-001

Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Operations

- Term: 24 months
- Committed spend: $420,000/year (billed annually)
- Effective discount: 30% (as modeled per Vanessa's worksheet)
- Deliverables: final quote, DocuSign signature, AWS private offer submission by Redwood Sales Ops

1) Sign the attached DocuSign (redwood-final-quote-BW-2026.pdf).
2) Send PO (if required) to orders@redwood.com referencing DEAL-BW-2026-001.
3) We will submit the private offer to AWS Seller Central once DocuSign is complete and provide the private offer link for you to accept.

If everything looks good, Vanessa / Marcus and I will coordinate the AWS private offer submission and target a March 1 effective date.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
